learning_objective: 🎯 Understand networking architectures, scale classifications (PAN to WAN), transmission media, hardware devices, and network topologies.

key_vocabulary.definition: A collection of interconnected computing devices capable of exchanging data and sharing resources.
The geometric arrangement or physical layout of connected devices and links in a network.
The maximum data transfer rate of a network channel, typically measured in bits per second (bps).
Media Access Control Address: A unique 48-bit physical address permanently assigned to a Network Interface Card (NIC).

main_concepts.simple_explanation: 1) **PAN (Personal Area Network):** Within ~10 meters (e.g., Bluetooth devices). 2) **LAN (Local Area Network):** Within a room, building, or campus (~1 km). 3) **MAN (Metropolitan Area Network):** Across a city (~50 km, e.g., Cable TV). 4) **WAN (Wide Area Network):** Spans countries or continents (e.g., The Internet).

1) **Wired (Guided):** Twisted Pair (Ethernet cables, cheapest), Coaxial Cable (TV networks), and Optical Fiber (light pulses, fastest, immunity to electromagnetic interference). 2) **Wireless (Unguided):** Radio Waves (omnidirectional), Microwaves (line-of-sight), and Infrared (short distance, obstructed by walls).

1) **Hub:** A dumb multiport device that broadcasts incoming packets to all connected devices. 2) **Switch:** An intelligent device that forwards packets ONLY to the destination MAC address. 3) **Router:** Connects different networks and finds the optimal path for IP packets. 4) **Modem:** Modulates digital signals to analog and demodulates analog back to digital for telephone line transmission.

1) **Bus:** All devices share a single backbone cable; easy to set up but fails if backbone breaks. 2) **Star:** All nodes connect to a central switch; highly reliable (node failure doesn't crash network). 3) **Tree:** A hierarchical combination of Bus and Star topologies. 4) **Mesh:** Every node connects to every other node; most redundant and expensive.

exam_tips: 📌 In network design case-study questions: always place the **Server** in the building/wing with the **maximum number of computers**.
📌 Always suggest a **Switch** to interconnect computers within a building, and a **Router/Modem** to connect a campus to the Internet or an external WAN.
📌 For interconnecting buildings more than 100 meters apart on a campus, recommend **Optical Fiber** (if budget allows) or **Radio/Microwave links** (if terrain is difficult/hilly).
quick_recap: ⭐ A Star Topology is the industry standard for modern LANs due to ease of troubleshooting and fault isolation.
⭐ A Repeater is an active device used to regenerate and amplify signals when cable length exceeds maximum transmission distance (~100m for Ethernet).
⭐ Optical fibers use Total Internal Reflection (TIR) to transmit data at the speed of light.
